structure.heading: FY2025 Consolidated Financial Performance and Earnings Drivers
text_content: **FY2025 Consolidated Financial Performance and Earnings Drivers**

The company reported consolidated full-year revenue of $18.6 billion for FY2025 ended December 31, 2025, delivering a year characterized by solid top-line growth and disciplined cost management. Operating margin was 16.2% in FY2025, reflecting margin expansion driven by product mix improvement and manufacturing efficiencies across the portfolio. Diluted earnings per share for the year were $3.48, underscoring strong net income conversion and stable capital structure. These outcomes support a resilient financial profile amid macro volatility in 2025.

Revenue and margin performance were driven by three primary factors: (1) sustained demand for higher-margin software and services offerings, (2) ongoing productivity initiatives in manufacturing and logistics, and (3) disciplined go-to-market execution in North America and Europe. Cost discipline reduced variable and fixed overhead, contributing to the 16.2% operating margin. The company’s capital structure and share count dynamics supported diluted EPS of $3.48, with the Board maintaining focus on shareholder value creation.

Strong cash generation in FY2025 enabled continued investment in R&D and selective capital expenditures while preserving balance sheet flexibility as of December 31, 2025. Management prioritized a balanced capital allocation framework that includes dividends, opportunistic share repurchases, and strategic M&A to enhance long-term EPS accretion. Investors should note that forward-looking targets and detailed FY2026 assumptions are presented in the 'Segment Results and FY2026 Investor Guidance with Key Assumptions' section for a comprehensive outlook.

structure.heading: Segment Results and FY2026 Investor Guidance with Key Assumptions
text_content: **Segment Results and FY2026 Investor Guidance with Key Assumptions**

In FY2025, the Cloud & Subscriptions business delivered revenue of $7.9 billion, reflecting continued customer migration to subscription models and increased enterprise adoption of our platform services. Year-over-year expansion was driven by higher recurring-license uptake, professional services attachment, and stronger retention in the second half of the fiscal year. Management attributes resilience to expanded data-center footprint, multi-region availability announced in Q3 FY2025, and strategic partnerships, notably with leading systems integrators.

Industrial Solutions achieved an operating margin of 18.4% in FY2025, supported by product mix optimization and disciplined supply-chain execution. Cost-management initiatives introduced in Q1 FY2025 reduced variable manufacturing expenses and improved gross margin contribution despite component shortages in H1. Segment backlog strengthened across energy and automation portfolios, with targeted pricing actions offsetting commodity inflation; capital allocation prioritized tooling and service expansion to sustain margin profile into FY2026.
